fields.title: Data Subject Requests
fields.keyTakeaway: Self-service covers most requests and is cheaper than manual processing, and without a systems map, collecting a person's data turns into an investigation.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: A request arrives: "provide all my data." How much time will it take?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: Data subject requests have legal deadlines — usually 30 days. A product without a process fulfills them manually, and a single request eats up days of work. With a growing number of requests this becomes a permanent load.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Typical rights of a person regarding their data:
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: *Access.* Get a copy of what is stored about them. *Correction.* Change incorrect data. *Deletion.* Covered above. *Portability.* Get in a machine-readable format. *Objection.* Prohibit processing for specific purposes. *Consent withdrawal.* Stop what was done based on consent.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: What the product needs for this to work:
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Intake point.** A form or address known to the user. A request arriving in support chat is also a request — employees must recognize it.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **Identity confirmation.** Giving data to the wrong person is a leak. The verification method must exist, and it should not require new data.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **Inventory.** Where a person's data lives. Without a systems map, gathering turns into an investigation.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: **Automation.** A "download my data" button in the interface covers most requests on its own.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: **Deadline and tracking.** Request registration, deadline control.
fields.sections/2/blocks/8/text: Practical observation: **self-service is cheaper than processing.** Data export and account deletion in the interface remove most requests and improve the product along the way.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Self-service in profile: "Download my data" and "Delete account".
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: Export is generated asynchronously, arrives via link, contains profile, order history, reviews, consents. Format — JSON and CSV files.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Over a quarter: 340 self-service exports, 11 requests via support. Before the button appeared there were about 60 support requests per quarter, each taking 2–3 hours.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Identity confirmation for requests via support — via account login. If the person cannot log in — procedure via the same phone number.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Inventory: a map of six systems where a person's data might be — main database, analytics, search index, mailing system, support, payment provider. Updated when connecting a new system.
fields.sections/3/blocks/5/text: Tracking: requests are registered, 30-day deadline, notification 7 days before expiration. Over two years, not a single overdue one.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Export must contain data, not everything indiscriminately: technical logs and internal scores are usually excluded. Composition is determined with a lawyer.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Self-service covers most requests and is cheaper than manual processing, and without a systems map, collecting a person's data turns into an investigation.
